title: Looking for Work
goal: Ask about an opening, explain the work you want, and answer initial questions about experience and availability.

runs.text: A
job opening
or
vacancy
is a position available to fill. A
job posting
advertises a position. A
recruiter
works on finding or assessing candidates; an
employment agency
helps connect job seekers and work opportunities.
Experience
is work or activity you have done;
availability
is when you can work.
This fictional posting provides the facts for practice:

paragraphs.text: 16 hours a week, including Saturday afternoons. Help customers and organize shelves. Customer-service experience preferred. Ask the store manager for application instructions.

runs.text: Preferred
means wanted or favored in this posting;
required
would state a condition the employer says applicants must meet. Clarify any important uncertainty rather than guessing.

blocks.caption: Read a short posting · Applicant & Manager

runs.text: Still open?
checks whether the advertised position remains available.
How do I apply?
asks for the next process step; it does not commit you to accepting an eventual offer.
I'm looking for a part-time customer-service job
gives a role and work arrangement. You can add
I'd prefer evening shifts
I'm available on weekends
, or
I'm interested in an entry-level role
Entry-level
describes a beginning position in a field; the actual posting determines its requirements.

turns.speaker: Recruiter

runs.text: What kind of work are you looking for?

turns.en: What kind of work are you looking for?

turns.speaker: Job seeker

runs.text: Part-time retail work. I worked in a café for a year.

turns.en: Part-time retail work. I worked in a café for a year.

turns.speaker: Recruiter

runs.text: What experience do you have with customers?

turns.en: What experience do you have with customers?

turns.speaker: Job seeker

runs.text: I took orders, answered questions and handled busy periods.

turns.en: I took orders, answered questions and handled busy periods.

runs.text: When are you available?

turns.speaker: Job seeker

runs.text: Afternoons and weekends. I have classes in the mornings.

turns.en: Afternoons and weekends. I have classes in the mornings.

blocks.caption: Describe what you are seeking · Recruiter & Job seeker

runs.text: Retail
concerns selling goods to customers.
Handle busy periods
explains coping with a rush, but a concrete example is stronger than that phrase alone. You can describe a transferable skill even if the setting changes:
I haven't worked in a bookstore, but I have experience helping customers
Possible questions include
What skills do you have?
What pay are you looking for?
When could you start?
, and
Why did you leave your last job?
Supplied answers include
I could start next month
I'd like to understand the pay range first
, and
My previous job was temporary
If you need more information:
Could you tell me more about the responsibilities?
If you cannot meet the proposed hours:
I can't work mornings. Are there other shifts?
If the opening is filled:
Thanks for letting me know. Do you expect other openings?
Alone, read recruiter questions and answer from the role facts. Then rehearse both parts.
Ask about Maple Books' opening and schedule. Your role can work Saturdays but wants confirmation of the other hours.
Use this role: one year of previous café work; customer orders and questions; afternoons and weekends; can start next month. Answer the recruiter from the model.
The recruiter offers mornings only. Explain your limitation and ask about another shift. Alternatively, the position is filled; ask about future openings.
Sample possibilities:

“Is the position still open? What other hours would I work?” / “I worked in a café for a year. I helped customers and took orders. I'm available afternoons and weekends.” / “I can't work mornings. Are there afternoon shifts?” / “Do you expect any other openings?”
Later, change the role and availability. Check that you separated the work you want, the experience you actually have, and the employer's stated requirements.

ja: 希望と経験を、短く伝える。
note: 求人がまだ募集中かを確認します。働ける時間と、過去の経験を区別し、ない経験をあるように話す必要はありません。
